text:
anya: Heads-up — I'm seeing a consistent TTFT regression (~15-20%) on replay harness runs after the kernel selector change landed. Happening on medium-length sequences (~256) with KV cache warmup. Posting the short repro and profiler snapshot I ran.

sam: ugh. which selector change? the heuristics->throughput-prioritization one? :thinking:

anya: yep. PR #4182. It prefers fused attention kernels for short contexts but seems to pick them even when KV cache is hot and prefix reuse is high. Replay harness showed longer single-request tails.

devon: can you paste the profiling sample? quick glance might help identify where time is going.

anya: here's a trimmed perf sample (hot lines):
```
kernel_select_time_ms: 0.8
fused_attention_forward: 72.4%   (avg 3.2ms / call)
kv_cache_lookup: 4.1%
cross_stream_lock_wait: 9.9%
batching_window_flush: 6.0%
other: 7.6%
```
Notable: fused attention has higher per-call latency on these sequences when run with cached KV vs the slower but cheaper baseline kernel.

beth: that aligns with an earlier microbenchmark — fused kernels sometimes lose when sequence distribution has high prefix reuse because they can't re-use internal buffers efficiently. Did you compare goodput vs QPS? If goodput (useful tokens/sec) drops but QPS stays same, it's batching waste.

anya: yes: replay harness numbers:
- QPS: ~420 -> 430 (up slightly)
- p95 TTFT: 62ms -> 76ms (regression)
- TPOT 95: dropped by ~12%
- goodput tokens/sec: -14%
So stacking small latency increases per token into larger TTFT at p95.

perf-bot: :rotating_light: perf-regression-alert PR #4182 triggered: p95 TTFT increased 22% on replay suite (sha abcd123). See /perf/runs/2026-03-15/4182

sam: interesting that QPS went up but goodput down — suggests batching heuristics changed such that more tiny batches are being coalesced but each has worse kernel perf. Can you share batching window / policy used by the replay job?

anya: replay harness config snippet:
```
batching_policy: dynamic
max_batch_ms: 12
min_batch_qps_weight: 0.2
kv_warmup_prefetch: true
```
I toggled `max_batch_ms` to 8 in a separate run and p95 improved ~6ms but goodput still below baseline.

devon: hypothesis: kernel selection is ignoring estimated kernel variance under cached KV paths. We need a small microbenchmark: run two kernels (fused vs baseline) with warm KV warmups and identical batching windows — measure per-token latency and stddev across prefixes.

beth: Agreed. Also check if the selector's cost model uses sequence length only and not KV hit ratio. If it's blind to cache hit rate it will choose wrong kernel for replays that warm prefixes.

anya: ran microbench today — summary:
- fused kernel mean token latency: 0.0128ms (cold), 0.0135ms (warm)
- baseline kernel mean: 0.0140ms (cold), 0.0118ms (warm)
So baseline wins with warm KV.

sam: that's the smoking gun. The selector should incorporate an estimate for KV cache hit probability and amortized reuse. We also need to log TPOT (tokens-per-second per model pipeline) alongside TTFT so we can detect cases where QPS deceptive.

devon: actionable plan:
1) revert selector default to conservative baseline for replay-suite A/B runs (canary) — reduces risk.
2) extend selector feature vector with `kv_hit_estimate` and `batching_window_ms` and retrain cost model.
3) add a replay-run metric hook: report goodput, TPOT, QPS, and TTFT p50/p95/p99 in one dashboard tile.

beth: minor: include an rr-window for warmup skew detection — compute prefix reuse ratio across replay traffic. If >0.6, prefer baseline kernel.

anya: I'll open a follow-up PR with (1) canary rollback for selector on replay runs and (2) a microbenchmark script and data. Dropping notes into the perf ticket.

perf-bot: :white_check_mark: benchmark-job queued: /bench/selector-kv-warmup/2250012345-run1 (ETA 40m)

sam: thanks. once we have run data let's re-evaluate with apples-to-apples: same batching policy, same traffic timeline — synthetic vs replay — to ensure we're not conflating sampler artifacts.

anya: will do. TL;DR: regression caused by kernel chooser ignoring KV-warm path; QPS can mask goodput loss, so dashboards must show both TPOT/goodput and QPS. Also add automated regression guard on p95 TTFT and TPOT 95.
